I made this yesterday, and was inspired to post the recipe today. This can be pureed with broth to make a mushroom soup, mixed into an omelette, added as a pizza topping, the possibilities are endless! You can use fancy ingredients (pancetta, shallots, madeira) or keep it cheap; either way, it's simple.

1 T. Olive Oil 1/4 lb. Bacon or pancetta, coarsely chopped 1 1/4 lb. Mixed mushrooms (I've used shitake, button, baby bellas - whatever's on sale), stemmed and thinly sliced 1 Medium shallot or 1/4 Vidalia Onion - minced and 1 tbsp. minced garlic 1/4 c. Sherry, Madeira or dry red wine 1 c. Heavy Cream Salt & Pepper to taste

  1. Heat oil in a skillet and add bacon. Cook until bacon is brown and fat rendered; remove bacon and drain on a paper towel.
  2. Add mushrooms to skillet and cook in the fat until mushrooms are brown and soft, about 8 minutes (I cook on medium low).
  3. Add shallot and cook until shallot is soft, maybe another 5 minutes.
  4. Add wine, cook until wine has completely evaporated.
  5. Stir in cream and bacon bits/pancetta.

It makes me usually 3 cups of this stuff. I'll freeze it in two-cup containers and use whenever I need an easy dinner. To make as soup: Puree in a blender and add chicken broth until you get the thickness you would like & heat. Mushroom Risotto: Puree and add to finish off risotto. It's hard to say how much because I usually only do this for a family of two, and we only need maybe 1/2 cup of this at a time.

This stuff is earthy, hearty savory . . . amazing. And really only costs a few dollars for several meals.
